The [official protocol definition](https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/master/doc/PROTOCOL-HTTP2.md) mentions the `"grpc-timeout"` header which is a way for the client to tell the server what deadline it has.
As I understand it, the timeout should be converted into a deadline as soon as the header is read (before the rest of the payload).

Using this, when the server is overloaded, requests can just be dropped with `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` or `CANCELLED` (not sure which one should be picked on the server side) if it takes too long until they are processed.
E.g. in C++, There is the [`ServerContext::IsCancelled()`](https://grpc.github.io/grpc/cpp/classgrpc__impl_1_1_server_context.html#ac0fe2a9425b18b724f910adbe0e3c17a) function which can be used to exit early: [Blog post on gRPC deadlines](https://grpc.io/blog/deadlines/)

title: Fix client connection deadlock [closes #326]
body:
I think I'm starting to get a picture of the problem, here. (Please correct me if I'm wrong.)

`share::RecvStream` holds a `streams::OpaqueStreamRef` (via `share::ReleaseCapacity`). The `OpaqueStreamRef` is one of the structs that can hold a reference on the `Arc`. The other struct is `streams::StreamRef` (which in turn has an inner `OpaqueStreamRef`).

Here's an ASCII art diagram showing the hierarchy (as I understand it):

```
Process
└── share::RecvStream
    └── share::ReleaseCapacity
        └── streams::OpaqueStreamRef
            └── streams::Streams

client.handshake
└── client::Builder
    └── client::Handshake
        └── client::Connection
            └── proto::Connection
                └── streams::Streams
```

`Process` is a struct in the client example. `streams::Streams.has_streams_or_other_references` is where `Arc::strong_count`is called: https://github.com/carllerche/h2/blob/c7d4182ffec23bc1f508a62bb59a9c286fdc888a/src/proto/streams/streams.rs#L750-L761

Commenting these checks does indeed prevent the hang...

The race occurs when the `proto::Connection` future is polled prior to the `OpaqueStreamRef` being fully dropped. This happens because there are two futures in the client example; `client::Connection` and `Process` that both share a reference to the `streams::Streams`. Which means that success depends on the order which the two futures are polled.

From this perspective, I looked into how `proto::Connection` gets woken up, and it simply happens here when the `OpaqueStreamRef` is dropped: https://github.com/carllerche/h2/blob/c7d4182ffec23bc1f508a62bb59a9c286fdc888a/src/proto/streams/streams.rs#L1111-L1119

So the question I had, seeing this condition, is how can I check if all streams are closed on the connection? Well, this looks relevant: https://github.com/carllerche/h2/blob/cf62b783e0bfe7b183cdef78874c5ca6e417c59e/src/proto/streams/store.rs#L196-L198

And the patch works!

I don't know of a good way to test this, other than the STR in https://github.com/carllerche/h2/issues/326#issuecomment-441820232 ... Perhaps creating the two (or more) futures and polling them in deterministic order (instead of on the default tokio runtime) could surface the case where `proto::Connection.go_away.should_close_on_idle` returns false. But I can't see an obvious way to set it up without a large test fixture and set of mocks.

Because I can't deterministically test it, I honestly don't know if this is the right way to address the issue...

title: Should Payload data be `Buf` instead of `AsRef<[u8]>`?
body:
The current `Payload` trait only requires that chunks be able to represent a slice of bytes. There may be cases where a user has several non-contiguous slices they would like to send. The `Buf` trait makes it possible to represent those as a single chunk, without having to copy to a single contiguous array. Additionally, `AsyncWrite::write_buf` can use that knowledge to call `writev`.

Currently, in that situation, a user must either copy all the data into 1 buffer before sending to hyper, or send multiple chunks. hyper *will* by default not merge the chunks, and try to use `writev` itself, so users can already benefit. However, that benefit may not be obvious. I'm wondering if allowing the chunk to be a `Buf` itself would be more obvious.

Some potential downsides: it's a little more complicated to implement a custom `Buf` than a `AsRef<[u8]>`, though the common types already do. Additionally, it ties API compatibility to the `Buf` trait, which is expect to have some breaking changes. However, hyper already publicly exposes a dependency on `Bytes` from the same crate, and `AsyncWrite` which also depends on `Buf`, so probably not a big deal.

/cc @scottlamb

title: Avoid socket thrash
body: Hi, we're experiencing an issue with the latest version of `hyper` where lots of sockets are being placed in time-wait during periods of high load / high re-use of connections. The problem is due to the race between the `checkout` and `connect` futures. If an idle connection is returned to the pool, the `checkout` future will resolve and the `connect` future will be dropped. If the `connect` future has started establishing a connection on a socket, that socket will be closed and enter time-wait state. So if the time to establish a new connection is `X` and time to finish a request is `Y`, if `X > Y` a new connection will be discarded. Also the ratio of `X / Y` is the factor that must be exceeded by concurrent requests in order to change the number of connections, so if a request finishes in ~0.05s and a new connection takes ~0.5s to establish then any increase of load greater than your current number of connections (up to 10x) will cause up to ~9x connections to be created and closed. ``` (Above) A spike in socket churn during high load. Yellow: TCP time-wait sockets. Green: TCP in-use sockets. ``` --- My original approach was to race the `checkout` against a shortened `connect` future which is just the connector's `connect()` future. This didn't work because the `connect()` future returned by the `Connector` begins the process of establishing a connection on the socket in the middle of the future. So ideally we would be able to race the checkout until a socket is chosen for connection, but this would change the `Connect` trait API so I wasn't sure if it was the right change to make. Instead I set the checkout future to just check if an idle connection was ready or return `err_canceled`. This way if the `avoid_socket_thrash` variable is set, the `checkout` future will always win the race and will return a `Pooled` if it exists or else run the `connect` future.

title: Assorted fixes to subquery regressions in 1.6
body:
This fixes two problems in subqueries that were introduced in 1.6. The first is that using a function on a tag when the tag was in a subquery such as the following:

    SELECT count(host) FROM (SELECT value, host FROM cpu)

This was previously allowed, but during a refactor, I forgot to treat tags as strings when reading from a subquery result so it would discard the results rather than read from them as if it were a string.

The second is that tags were not stripped from subqueries when the outer query did not group by that tag as in this example:

    SELECT value FROM (SELECT value FROM cpu GROUP BY host)

Both of these regressions have been fixed and test cases have been added.

title: time for calculated query answers needs to reflect actual data
body:
When influxdb is used to select an individual result, the time associated with it is returned. e.g., if I do:

SELECT LAST(x) FROM table WHERE ... time > now() - 1d ....

then influxdb will give me output with the timestamp set to the last row from "table".

However if I do a query like this:

SELECT MAX(x) - MIN(x) FROM table WHERE ... time > now() - 1d ....

then influxdb uses the value of "now() - 1d" as the timestamp for the result "MAX(x) - MIN(x)". This is not useful as it cannot be aligned with any other timestamps in influxdb.

Ideally the timestamp for "MAX(x) - MIN(x)" would come from the actual timestamp of either the row for MAX(x) or MIN(x), not "now() - 1d"/"now()".

title: Poor performance on last()

<!--

Thank you for reporting a bug in InfluxDB. 

* Please ask usage questions on the Influx Community site.
    * https://community.influxdata.com/

__Steps to reproduce:__
List the minimal actions needed to reproduce the behavior.

1. Fill a database with a lot of data
2. Query it using last()
3. Wait a long time

__Expected behavior:__
Describe what you expected to happen.

Querying the last value of a given field should be a constant-time lookup.

__Actual behavior:__
Describe What actually happened.

Instead, influx takes increasingly longer to find the last value with more points.

A database containing just 3 million points, the query `select last("my_field") as "last_field" from "my_measurement"` has in some cases taken up to 6 hours to complete, but on average takes about 3 minutes. 

While this query executes, it uses 100% of all four cores and makes InfluxDB completely unresponsive until the query has finished executing.

Judging roughly based on the quadratic curve of the queryDurationNs field in the queryExecutor measure, it appears to be ~O(n^2) to calculate this last point. 

The poor performance of this function makes it difficult to use on medium-sized datasets.

I'm trying to determine the last timestamp a measurement was written to in order to differentially load data into InfluxDB from another database. After searching for a way to do this in a more traditional way, like selecting max(time), I determined that the `last()` InfluxQL function is the only way to do this. title: Add options to group by time to set where the time windows occur
body:
Currently when you do a query and `GROUP BY time(1h)` it will bucket everything modulo the interval, directly on the hour markers. Users should be able to specify that the buckets occur either at the current time, or some offset, or the time of the first or last data point in a query, like so:

``` sql
SELECT mean(value)
FROM cpu
WHERE time > now() - 10h
GROUP BY time(10m, now())

-- or this
SELECT mean(value)
FROM cpu
WHERE time > now() - 10h
GROUP BY time(10m, last())

-- or this
SELECT mean(value)
FROM cpu
WHERE time > now() - 10h and time < now() - 1h
GROUP BY time(10m, now() - 1h)

-- or this
SELECT mean(value)
FROM cpu
WHERE time > now() - 10h
GROUP BY time(10m, first())
```

These options to the group by time will only be valid for live queries. If someone is creating a continuous query we'll have to validate that they haven't put in these extra options.

title: UI Link between Notification Rule and Checks
body:
__Proposal:__
InfluxDB v2. The Notification Rule dialog should include a multi-selectable hyperlinked list of checks to which it applies.

__Current behavior:__
Notification Rules are currently global. If you want to restrict a notification rule to a more limited set of checks, you need to go to each check, define a tag name & value, return to the notification rule and add a tag filter.
There is no option to check validity of the tag name or value from the notification rule. There is no way to see what checks define a specific tag without going into the configuration of each one. Similarly, there is no way to identify the checks that use a specific tag, and there is no way to identify the notification rules that will fire on a check.

__Desired behavior:__
If there was a clickable list of checks (with a "select all" and "select none" added) in the Notification Rule dialog, it would be obvious which checks are relevant for a notification rule. Similarly, if there was a list of notification rules in the check dialog, it would be obvious which notification rules were applied to a check.

__Alternatives considered:__
I've tried to use the current functionality of the manual creation of tags in every check, remembering which tag names and values I've used, and writing them as filters in each notification rule. It's a lot of work.

__Use case:__
This would improve UX, replacing lots of typing with a couple of button presses. The current behaviour was also mentioned by a prospect as being an unexpected limitation.

title: Add ability to Merge/Stack Telegraf configurations in UI
body:
### Use case
Installing multiple templates from which each Telegraf configuration is needed in the same data source.  

Example: 

User has a K8s-centric infrastructure.  They want to run Telegraf as a daemonset and want to use Templates to get started.  They use Redis, Nginx, HAproxy, Kafka, MySQL, etc., and want to take advantage of the templated Telegraf configurations that exist for each of these services.  

### Problem: 
Complete Telegraf configurations are in each Template.  User's ability to combine these configurations is hindered.  

Their options become:
- Running Telegraf with multiple local configurations
  - `telegraf.d/` currently only works with local configs and the idea behind the Telegraf/2.0 duality is managing and obtaining configuration from a central InfluxDB repository.  Even locally, this method shares the other issues.
- Running multiple Telegrafs on the same data source
  - IMO, this is clunky and will be an oft-rejected pattern for users 
- Copy/pasting relevant diffs of multiple configs into one
  - Too manual and degrades the overall InfluxDB Templates messaging of time-to-awesome and one-command utility
- Copy/paste parts of multiple config files into one

#### Separate problem (addressed in proposed solution):
The most part of authoring a template is including even one Telegraf configuration.  It requires manually entering boilerplate YAML and pasting your TOML into that section.  From there, the author must make sure all lines are properly indented.  I think it's safe to this isn't the experience we want for users of any piece of InfluxData software.

### Proposal
Editable configurations in UI.  Ultimately, the envisioned UX of this to have some kind of UI for moving configuration blocks between configuration files.  This would mean the UI understands the components of the config files and exposes them as objects that can be moved, copied, picked from a dropdown or checked/selected in a list, etc.  

The idea here is to benefit both the Template author and consumer personas.  If the Template author can create and edit configuration in the UI, they can export (generate this portion of the template) right from their workspace.  

#### Some possible additions to this (needs more discussion and validation)
- Templates repo enforces a lack of agent and output configuration.  The UI would supply a default Agent for all configurations to share.  This could be copied and then edited for custom Agent configurations( adding jitter, changing intervals and batching, enabling debug, etc.).  The output plugin would also be provided/generated.  We would then leave the option of using non-InfuxDB outputs to the template user if needed (outside of template).

Workflow change for author:
- Author can now create and modify configuration from the UI and export from there which skips a couple steps!
- Author is now encouraged to include a `namepass` field in any Processor/Aggregator plugins they use.  This is because they will only expect the input data from the Template for which they were written.  When combined with inputs from other Templates, we'd like to avoid the necessary overhead of each of those plugins dealing with more data than they need to.
- (only if Agent/Output exclusion is enforced) Do not include Agent or Output configurations


Workflow change for consumer:
- Instead of copy/pasting piecemealed configuration and 


#### Alternatives proposed
1. Telegraf would support intelligently merging configurations based on diffs.  There is an assumption that the Agent configuration blocks are 
    - Deemed out of scope
2.  Telegraf would support running with multiple remote configurations (like `telegraf.d/` but for centrally hosted configs in, say Influx2)
    - Could have added a flag like `--config-url` to pull multiple configs.  
    - This does not fully eliminate challenges with config overlap, conflicts, etc.

title: stddev() function crashes on large data sets
body: I have stumbled across some problems with Influx's stddev() function. By way of background, I have an ESP8266-based monitor sampling grid voltage at 10-second intervals, logging via Mosquitto and Node-Red into InfluxDB 1.8.4 running inside a Docker container on a 4GB Raspberry Pi 4B with a 500MB SSD. The database is approximately 3 years old and has over 9 million rows. Recently, I wanted to calculate the voltage mean and standard deviation, but the container crashed. The crash was *repeatable* and that led me to investigate further. My findings suggest that Influx's stddev() function is probably implemented in a fairly inefficient fashion, is consuming huge amounts of memory unnecessarily and, on large data sets, is likely to crash with the error: ``` fatal error: out of memory ``` ## summary of test results stddev() crashing on large data sets is probably just a symptom. I suspect the underlying problem will be found in the algorithm being used to calculate standard deviations. To try to demonstrate that "something strange is going on", I needed comparison tests. I used SQLite because it was handy, I was familiar with it, I already had it running on the same hardware, I could easily load the same data into it, and both it and Influx implement roughly similar 4GL front ends. It was simply the closest I could get to a reasonably fair basis for meaningful comparison. *Nothing else should be read into this choice.* In the table below, each "Test Group" refers to the size of the result set (ie the value to the right of "count" in each grouping). See [influx\_tests](#influxTests) for an expanded definition. The original voltage data is recorded to 1 decimal place. Results in this table are rounded to two decimal places. ![Timings](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/34226495/111106704-b6562c00-85a9-11eb-8a62-9e62ebf1466a.png) > † The overall elapsed time for running the Influx test suite was 4:49.47. Subtracting the other values in the "Influx Time" column leaves 0:32.06 which implies the stddev() function crashed approximately 32 seconds into the calculation. Definition of values in "Test" column: * *count:* count(), both Influx and SQLite * *mean:* Influx mean(), SQLite avg() * *sumSq:* sum(voltage*voltage), indirect via sub-select for Influx, direct for SQLite * *calc:* inline calculation of sample standard deviation using this formula: ![sampleStandardDeviationComputational](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/34226495/111105319-ce787c00-85a6-11eb-872d-2c3e6cd42269.png) * *stddev:* Influx stddev() function (no equivalent for SQLite) Key points: 1. The [raw test results](#rawTestResults) show that the inline calculations and stddev() functions return the same answer (to many more decimal places). In other words, there is no evidence to conclude that either the inline calculation or stddev() function is either "incorrect" or "more correct" in any mathematical or statistical sense. 2. The fact that the inline calculation can compute the standard deviation for the 9M records case, while the stddev() function crashes, shows that there is no particular reason why stddev() should need a lot of memory. 3. The "calc" rows show *significant* timing differences between Influx and SQLite. For example, 84 seconds for Influx vs 4 seconds for SQLite, to calculate the 9M records case. This is due to a minor implementation difference and was a conscious choice to make the point as to how the stddev() function was likely to be going about its work. There is more detail at [inline calculation differences](#inlineCalculations). The following chart displays the timing results from the above table: ![stddev-results](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/34226495/111105362-ea7c1d80-85a6-11eb-9ae6-b3d15293bca1.png) Key points: 1. The similarity of Influx timings for "Influx sumSq", "Influx calc" and "Influx stddev" li

title: Can we have IN filter?
SELECT * from two measurements with different fields fails
body:
If you have two measurements with different fields in them you get an error when doing a select \* query like this:

``` sql
SELECT * 
FROM s1, s2
```

It will give an error about a field not being defined. This is because the expansion of the `*` operator is happening before the query gets expanded into two statements, one for `s1` and one for `s2`

title: Count all points in a database
body:
__Proposal:__
Return the total amount of points in a database.

__Current behavior:__
Currently this is only possible by counting all points in each measurement in a database with `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "measurementName"` queries and then summing the results of those queries up. The bad thing about this is, that these queries can take a lot of time if there are a lot of points (several hundred millions, over a billion or even more). 

__Desired behavior:__
It would be much faster, if the total number of the points per database are already stored somewhere. Maybe in a measurement that exists per database and that is created by the InfluxDB service itself? This number should also be persisted and not reset to zero when the InfluxDB service restarts.

__Alternatives considered:__
A possible solution would also be to just return all written points without considering already deleted points. That would make things a bit easier I guess.

__Use case:__
For us this is important, because we want to be able to see quite fast, which databases actually hold a lot of points and which not. We do not fill the databases ourself. We provide InfluxDB databases to our users and the databases get created automatically if a user requests one on our self developed IoT platform.

Because of this, right now we have no quick and easy overview about which databases are actually used a lot and which not.

title: Broker checksum
body:
## Overview

This pull request changes the binary format of `messaging.Message` to encode a 4-byte checksum at the beginning of it. This is used when reading data back out to verify that it is not corrupt. Corrupted messages are truncated on recovery so the broker can restart from the previous message.

title: fix: detect misquoted tag values and return an error
body:
`SHOW TAG KEYS FROM "foo" where bar="misquoted"` is
erroneous, because the tag value must be enclosed
in single, not double, quotes. Although this
correctly returns no tag keys, it is very
inefficient and has caused out-of-memory failures
at a customer. This fix short-circuits the query and returns
an error. This fix also handles `SHOW TAG VALUES`
with a misquoted `WHERE` clause. 

Closes https://github.com/influxdata/influxdb/issues/22755

title: Need tool to migrate data from 0.8.x to 0.9
body:
As part of the release of 0.9.0 Final we need a migration utility that can port data from an 0.8.x datastore into 0.9.0. Because 0.8.x supported multiple underlying datastores we cannot simply transform the data on disk. We believe it will be easiest to "replay" the data from the 0.8.x server into the 0.9.0 server as a series of reads and writes. This means all data from 0.8.x needs to be turned into valid JSON for 0.9.0.

We assume that 0.8.x series names are of the format 

```
<tagName>.<tagValue>.[<tagName>.<tagValue>.]<measurement>
```

For example: 

```
zone.us-west-1.host.serverA.cpu_load_short
```

Note that migrations for 0.8.x schemas outside this default may require custom solutions.

The corresponding 0.9.0 series would presumably be defined with `measurement` as the series name and the key-value tag pairs turned into explicit tags on the series but not as part of the series name. 

Continuing our example:

```
zone.us-west-1.host.serverA.cpu_load_short
```

becomes (given in partial JSON format as if for a write)

```
"name": "cpu_load_short",
"tags": {
       "host": "serverA",
       "zone": "us-west"
},
```

The associated timestamps and values can be rewritten into the 0.9.0 database without transformation. 

This suggests that the migration tool should pop the measurement name off the end of the 0.8.x series name and use it is the series name in 0.9.0. The tool should also pull key-value pairs out of the 0.8.x series name and make them tags on the new series in 0.9.0. 

Note that we do need to be careful about precision on timestamps. Ideally we would preserve the original precision from the 0.8.x series. At a minimum we can convert all 0.8.x timestamps to RFC3339Nano for injection into 0.9.0.

title: write_lp HTTP API
body:
The v3 write API should be a POST to `/api/v3/write_lp`. There is a shell of this already in #24552. The parameters it should take are `db`, `precision`, `accept_partial`. Precision and token are optional. A bearer token can be provided via the Authorization header.

If precision is not supplied, when the line protocol is parsed, the server should guess at the precision of each line assuming that the passed in timestamp should be roughly around `now`. Thus it could accept second, millisecond, microsecond, and nanosecond and have the time be around now.

The `accept_partial` parameter specifies that the server should write any lines that are valid and return errors for any lines that are invalid. This defaults to true. If false, any invalid line will cause the entire request to error with no lines written. In either case, if there are any invalid lines, the server should return a 400.

The behavior behind this endpoint(some of this logic will reside in the buffer):
* Validate the db name contains only numbers, letters, underscores and hyphens. Must start with either a number or letter.
* Optionally take precision, with a default of `auto`
* Optionally take a bearer token (don't have to wire up auth as part of this issue)
* Create a database in the buffer if it doesn't exist
* Limit the number of databases to 5 (this is a hard limit, not user configurable)
* Limit the total number of tables across all databases to 2,000
* Limit the number of columns on any table to 500 (hard limit, not user configurable)
* Return an error JSON with any invalid lines

Invalid lines should not be written to the WAL (if a WAL is configured).

title: Support sub-queries containing qualified measurement names in InfluxQL `SELECT` statements
body:
This issue is for supporting sub-queries in an InfluxQL `SELECT` statement that contain qualified measurement names.

A qualified measurement name is one that contains the database name and retention policy, e.g.,
```
foo.autogen.bar
```
#### Components
* `foo`: database name (DB)
* `autogen`: retention policy (RP)
* `bar`: measurement name

#### Usage
```sql
SELECT * FROM foo.autogen.bar
```

We added support for `SELECT` queries that use qualified measurement names in the `FROM` clause in #24696, but the logic added there does not perform the extraction of DB or RP from any sub-query in the `FROM` clause.

This would need to be a recursive process, and we would need to put in some restrictions. Namely:

* sub-queries can only be performed on the same singular DB/RP as their parent

title: v1 write API
body:
Support the `/api/v1/write` API in Edge. Documentation for this API can be found [here](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/v1/tools/api/#write-http-endpoint).

## Requirements

This API is very similar to Edge's `/api/v3/write` API, with some differences:

* No `accept_partial` parameter
* The `precision` is defaulted to nanoseconds, vs. the auto-detection that `v3` has
* Supports the `p` and `u` parameters for authorization as well as basic authentication; we can follow the `query` API implementation by supporting the `p` for the token (#24754), but basic authentication will not be supported, and the `u` parameter will be ignored.
* `rp` parameter, if provided, will need to be factored into the database name that is used to perform the write
  
  For example, with `db=foo` and `rp=bar`, the underlying database written to would be `foo/bar`. If `rp` is `"default"` or `"autogen"`, it is ignored.
* A `consistency` parameter is accepted in the original API, but this will be ignored in Edge

## Other Notes

* The [status codes returned](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/v1/tools/api/#status-codes-and-responses-2) are fairly prescriptive, and we may need to follow these to preserve compatibility.

title: v2 write API
body:
Support the `/api/v2/write` API in Edge. Documentation for this API can be found [here](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/v2/api/#operation/PostWrite).

## Requirements

This API is very similar to the Edge's `/api/v3/write` API, with some differences:

* No `accept_partial` parameter
* The `precision` is defaulted to nanoseconds, vs. the auto-detection in `v3` - this is not explicit in the docs, but is clear from the code: https://github.com/influxdata/influxdb/blob/1baa393f692083f24e9181970ebc57391bc8e79f/http/write_handler.go#L249-L254
* The database name is passed in the `bucket` parameter. Some special attention is given to this parameter for v1 compatibility, see [here](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/v1/tools/api/#apiv2write-http-endpoint), so we may need to do some name wrangling with what is passed in this parameter; for now, it is probably okay to accept what is passed there as the database name.
* `org` and `orgId` parameters are ignored in Edge
* Supports compression of the body containing line protocol data via gzip

## Other Notes

* Authorization is done via API Tokens passed in the `Authorization` header as a `Bearer` token; so we can rely on 3.0's auth scheme.
* Status codes and error responses returned are specified and may need to be followed for compatibility

title: feat: support v1 and v2 write APIs
body:
Closes #24780
Closes #24781

This adds support for two APIs: `/write` and `/api/v2/write`. These implement the v1 and v2 write APIs, respectively. In general, the difference between these and the new `/api/v3/write_lp` API is in the request parsing. We leverage the `WriteRequestUnifier` trait from `influxdb3_core` to handle parsing of v1 and v2 HTTP requests, to keep the error handling at that level consistent with distributed versions of InfluxDB 3.0. Specifically, we use the `SingleTenantRequestUnifier` implementation of the trait.

### Changes:

* Addition of two new routes to the `route_request` method in `influxdb3_server::http` to serve `/write` and `/api/v2/write` requests.
* Database name validation was updated to handle cases where retention policies may be passed in `/write` requests, and to also reject empty names. A unit test was added to verify the `validate_db_name` function.
* HTTP request `authorization` in the router will extract the full `Authorization` header value, and store it in the request extensions; this is used in the write request parsing from the core `iox_http` crate to authorize write requests.
* E2E tests to verify correct HTTP request parsing / response behaviour for both `/write` and `/api/v2/write` APIs
* E2E tests to check that data sent in through `/write` and `/api/v2/write` can be queried back

### Other Notes

* This does not address any issues outlined in #24730 and does in fact allow writes to databases that have retention policies in their name, e.g., `"foo/bar"`, through the `/write` API.

title: Load generator tests on the last cache
body:
Once the last cache has been implemented we will want to run a series of load generator tests to see how it performs compared to SQL queries that would be used in its absence.

The only setup required in the load generator should be to create the specs that exercise the queries below. We could have the load generator create the last cache, but will probably just be easy enough to write some data in and create the cache using the CLI, before running the load gen tests.

## Scenarios

Here are some scenarios we want to test.

### 1. Basic last value queries

In this case, the cache does not need to be keyed on any columns.

#### Using SQL

```sql
SELECT * FROM 'table' ORDER BY time DESC LIMIT 1
```

#### Using Last Cache

```sql
SELECT * FROM last_cache('table')
```

### 2. Multi-level tag/key hierarchy

In this case, the data has a hierarchical tag set, e.g., `region/host/cpu`. The last cache is keyed using the hierarchy `region -> host -> cpu`, and we want to compare query performance when using different combinations of predicates.

#### Using SQL

In general, situations where attempting to pull the _N_-most-recent values for a set of time series, we can use a combination of a ranking function, e.g., `ROW_NUMBER()` and `PARTITION BY` like so:
```sql
WITH ranked AS (
   SELECT
      *,
      ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY host ORDER BY time DESC) AS rn
   FROM cpu
   WHERE <predicate>
)
SELECT * FROM ranked
WHERE rn <= N
```
Here, predicate can be, e.g.,
* `host IN ('_', '_', ...)`
* `region IN ('_', '_', ...)`
* `host = '_' AND cpu = '_'`
* `host = '_'`
* `region = '_'`
* etc.

#### Using Last Cache

Here, the last cache is doing the work for us, so we really just need to provide the above predicates like so:

```sql
SELECT * FROM last_cache('cpu') WHERE host IN ('_', '_', ...)
SELECT * FROM last_cache('cpu') WHERE region IN ('_', '_', ...)
SELECT * FROM last_cache('cpu') WHERE host = '_' AND cpu = '_'
SELECT * FROM last_cache('cpu') WHERE host = '_'
SELECT * FROM last_cache('cpu') WHERE region = '_'
```

title: feat: `last_caches` system table
body:
Closes #25098

Adds a new system table: `system.last_caches` to enable queries that display information about last caches in a database.

You can query the table like so:
```sql
SELECT * FROM system.last_caches
```
Since queries are scoped to a database, this will only show last caches configured for the database being queried.

Results look like so:
```
+-------+----------------+----------------+---------------+-------+-----+
| table | name           | key_columns    | value_columns | count | ttl |
+-------+----------------+----------------+---------------+-------+-----+
| mem   | mem_last_cache | [host, region] | [time, usage] | 1     | 60  |
+-------+----------------+----------------+---------------+-------+-----+
```

An end-to-end test was added to verify queries to the `system.last_caches` table.

title: E2E integration tests are flaky
body:
From time to time, some of the integration tests fail for strange reasons. It may be due to how a port is being selected for the running `influxdb3 serve` binary that is spun up in the test harness.

There is a function used to select a random available port: https://github.com/influxdata/influxdb/blob/7d37bbbce7ecd4f6c95445de2b22ee189dd93b85/influxdb3/tests/server/main.rs#L305-L319

However, since the bind address is dropped before it is passed in to spawn the server (it needs to be, otherwise the server would not be able to bind that address and would fail to start), then there is a chance that another process or integration test could take over that port before the binary is started here: https://github.com/influxdata/influxdb/blob/7d37bbbce7ecd4f6c95445de2b22ee189dd93b85/influxdb3/tests/server/main.rs#L136

title: feat: allow the specification of a write window for retention policies
body:
Add `FutureWriteLimit` and `PastWriteLimit` to 
retention policies. Points which are outside of
`now() + FutureWriteLimit`
or
`now() - PastWriteLimit`
will be rejected with a `PartialWriteError`.

Closes https://github.com/influxdata/influxdb/issues/25424

title: Certain combinations of filter expressions may produce unexpected query results
body:
As of now this is officially only a hunch, as there is no reproducer yet. But, my hunch is that with how the last cache is handling predicates, if a query contains multiple predicates on a single column, it will not properly handle them.

For example,
```sql
SELECT * FROM last_cache('foo') WHERE bar = 'baz' OR bar = 'bop'
```
will only evaluate using one of the `bar =` predicates, instead of both in combination.

The fix should be to combine expressions in such a scenario to become:
```sql
SELECT * FROM last_cache('foo') WHERE bar IN ('baz', 'bop')
```

Other scenarios that need to be considered are where multiple incompatible predicates are provided, for example,
```sql
SELECT * FROM last_cache('foo') WHERE bar = 'baz' AND bar = 'bop'
SELECT * FROM last_cache('foo') WHERE bar = 'baz' OR bar != 'baz'
```
Should either be an error, or ignored, so DataFusion can handle it.

title: Unhandled query errors in plugins should be logged or returned to user
body:

title: test: add reproducer that shows group by behaviour
body:
Related to #25751

This is a reproducer for what I think is a bug in the InfluxQL query planner/executor.

What this demonstrates is that when a regex is used in a `GROUP BY` in an InfluxQL query to select on groups of multiple tags, the tags that do not match the regex are not included in the projected query result.

However, if the same tags that would be matched by the regex are provided explicitly, the other columns are included in the projection.

See the test added in this PR.

title: feat: Implement `date_part` scalar function
body:
Implements `date_part(part, expression)`, which extracts a component from a timestamp.

Signature:

- Exactly 2 args, in order: `date_part('<part>', time)`
  - arg 1: string literal naming the part (case-insensitive)
  - arg 2: the `time` VarRef, nothing else
- Returns `int64`, evaluated in the query timezone (`tz(...)`), default UTC

Parts:

| part | value |
|------|-------|
| `year` | calendar year |
| `quarter` | quarter of year, `[1, 4]` |
| `month` | month of year, `[1, 12]` |
| `week` | ISO-8601 week of year, `[1, 53]` |
| `day` | day of month, `[1, 31]` |
| `hour` / `minute` / `second` | `[0,23]` / `[0,59]` / `[0,59]` |
| `millisecond` / `microsecond` / `nanosecond` | seconds-of-minute scaled to the unit plus the sub-second component, e.g. `45.123s` returns `45123` for `millisecond` |
| `dow` | day of week, Sunday = 0 to Saturday = 6 |
| `isodow` | ISO-8601 day of week, Monday = 1 to Sunday = 7 |
| `doy` | day of year, `[1, 366]` |
| `epoch` | seconds since Unix epoch (whole seconds) |

`week` is the ISO week and `year` is the calendar year, so the two can disagree at
year boundaries. For example 2023-01-01 returns week 52.

Examples:

```sql
-- weekdays only
SELECT * FROM some_measurement
WHERE time >= now() - 10d AND time <= now()
  AND date_part('dow', time) != 0 AND date_part('dow', time) != 6

SELECT value, date_part('hour', time) FROM some_measurement
```

SELECT rules

- Must be paired with an anchor, meaning a stored field or a non-`date_part`
  aggregate or selector. `date_part`-only selects are rejected.
- Multiple `date_part` fields and aliases are allowed, and may nest in expressions
  such as `date_part('hour', time) + 1`.

GROUP BY date_part rules

- Allowed alongside `time()`. Other calls in GROUP BY are rejected.
- Requires exactly one non-`date_part` aggregate or selector in the SELECT list.
  Raw selects and multiple aggregates are rejected.
- Duplicate parts are deduplicated.
- A SELECTed `date_part('part', time)` must match a grouped part. A non-grouped
  part is rejected because it is undefined for the bucket. A non-active grouped
  part yields null in that series.
- Output column is named after the canonical part such as `year`. A field or alias
  colliding with it is rejected.
- Resolved from the bucket value, not the row timestamp.
- `fill(none)` is always supported. `fill(null)` (the default) is supported for a
  bare GROUP BY date_part but rejected when combined with a `time()` interval; use
  `fill(none)`. `fill(previous)`, `fill(linear)`, and `fill(<value>)` are rejected.

Subqueries

- `date_part` is supported in the WHERE clause and in GROUP BY of a query over a
  subquery source, computed from the timestamps the subquery emits. `tz(...)` is
  honored.
- The anchor rule applies through subqueries: the innermost statement must select
  a stored field or a non-`date_part` aggregate or selector.

See influxdata/influxdb#27001 for 1.x limitations.

title: fix: release TSM cursor references once when a Flux query is cancelled
body:
On context cancellation storage/flux stopped waiting for a table's
consumer but closed the table anyway, so table.Close() could race
advance() on a dispatcher goroutine. Both reach KeyCursor.Close(), which
releases every location before clearing c.seeks, so each TSM file was
Unref'd twice. That leaves TSMReader.refsWG negative -- WaitGroup.Add
decrements before it panics -- poisoning the reader for the life of the
process and failing every later query against that shard.

Transfer ownership via the `used` CAS the table already has: claim the
table when no consumer can run, otherwise wait for done, which is then
guaranteed to close. Waiting unconditionally would deadlock, since
consecutiveTransport drops queued messages on error without Ack'ing them.
Also make KeyCursor.Close idempotent as a backstop, and release the
cursor stranded when an array cursor's reset() fails.

Closes: #27570

title: InfluxDB 3 Core: querying system.parquet_files with a table_name filter for a nonexistent table panics (expect("table exists"), parquet_files.rs:66)
body:
## Problem

Querying `system.parquet_files` with a `table_name` filter that does not match an existing table **panics the request thread**. The client gets an HTTP 200 with a truncated/empty body rather than an error, so it looks like a successful query that returned nothing.

## Reproduction

Against any database (here `mydb`), with no special setup — the table simply has to not exist:

```sh
curl -X POST "$INFLUX_URL/api/v3/query_sql" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"db":"mydb","q":"SELECT * FROM system.parquet_files WHERE table_name = '\''no_such_table_xyz'\''","format":"json"}'
```

Server log:

```
ERROR panic_logging: Thread panic panic_type="unknown" panic_message="table exists"
  panic_file="influxdb3_system_tables/src/parquet_files.rs" panic_line=66 panic_column=18
```

The response is HTTP 200 with an empty body. Through some clients the broken response surfaces instead as a transport error (Python `urllib` reports `IncompleteRead(0 bytes read)`).

## Cause

`influxdb3_system_tables/src/parquet_files.rs` takes the table name straight from the query filter and `expect()`s that it resolves:

```rust
let table_name = find_table_name_in_filter(filters);

let parquet_files = if let Some(table_name) = table_name {
    let table_id = self
        .buffer
        .catalog()
        .db_schema_by_id(&self.db_id)
        .expect("db exists")
        .table_name_to_id(Arc::clone(&table_name))
        .expect("table exists");     // <-- line 66
```

`table_name` here is untrusted user input from the `WHERE` clause, so `table_name_to_id` legitimately returns `None` for any name that isn't a current table. A user-supplied value should not be able to reach an `expect()`.

The unfiltered form (`SELECT * FROM system.parquet_files`) is fine — it takes the `else` branch and enumerates the catalog instead.

## How I hit it in practice

Not by typo'ing a table name. I have a maintenance job that drops a disposable table and then reports how many Parquet files that reclaimed:

1. `DELETE /api/v3/configure/table?db=mydb&table=chatty_table&hard_delete_at=now`
2. `SELECT count(1) FROM system.parquet_files WHERE table_name = 'chatty_table'`

Step 2 panics, because step 1 removed the table from the catalog. So the natural "measure what I just cleaned up" sequence hits this every time, and the job reports a failure for an operation that actually succeeded.

## Expected

`SELECT ... FROM system.parquet_files WHERE table_name = '<unknown>'` returns **zero rows**, the same as filtering any table on a value that matches nothing.

## Environment

- InfluxDB 3 Core **3.11.1**, revision `a95809c862448e050a2f6db3df202984e058bac3`
- Official `influxdb:3-core` Docker image, `--object-store file`
- Single node, reproduced repeatedly

## Note

The panic is per-request — the server stays up and other queries are unaffected. I verified the process was not restarted and no data was lost. It is a broken response and a scary log line rather than an outage.

title: shouldn't fail if the wal ends prematurely
body: The wal should reset to the last known request offset. This scenario will happen if the log append stopped half way, e.g. the size of the request was written but the request wasn't written. In that case it should reset the file offset to the end of the previous request

Using `mean()` in a query breaks the response format: there are more columns than values in the query response.

title: [feature request] Querying by tag across measurements should exclude measurements without the tag, not fail with an error
body:
I'm not sure if the behaviour I'm describing is a bug or intended behaviour; I couldn't get a clear consensus from the docs.

The problem is that when doing a query using a regexp for the series and matching against a tag, the query will fail if any of the matching series is missing the tag.
My expectation would be to instead return those series where there were a matching tag, and just ignoring those that didn't have the tag.

My use case for these kind of queries is when doing cleanup of the db. We have a couple of series with various names. Some of the series are attached to "assets", and thus have an "asset" tag. When one of these assets are removed from the system we also want to prune the data and remove all time series that have a matching "asset" tag.

Another issue with this behaviour is that it's too easy to write queries which works one day, and then fails the next day because a new separate time series had been added, missing a tag.
I'll demonstrate with an example:

```
curl -G http://localhost:8086/query --data-urlencode "q=CREATE DATABASE tagtest"
curl -i -XPOST 'http://localhost:8086/write?db=tagtest' --data-binary 'test_point,tag1=one value=1'
curl -G http://localhost:8086/query --data-urlencode "db=tagtest"  --data-urlencode "q=SELECT * FROM /.*/ where tag1='one'"
```

The last query for all series with the a tag of name "tag1" and value "1" will succeed.
However, if another time series is added without the tag, and the same query is run again it will fail:

```
curl -i -XPOST 'http://localhost:8086/write?db=tagtest' --data-binary 'test_point_without_tag value=1'
curl -G http://localhost:8086/query --data-urlencode "db=tagtest"  --data-urlencode "q=SELECT * FROM /.*/ where tag1='one'"
```

title: Period in field name that matches measurement fails.  Fixes #3457
body:
fixes #3457

We had some code that used to check to see if we asked for a `measurement.fieldname` in a select statement.  Even though we were apparently `normalizing` this, we don't actually look this back up on the query engine, so effectively it did nothing.

The scenario it should of accounted for was given:

```
insert cpu value=1
insert memory value=2
```

That the following query would work:

```
select cpu.value, memory.value from cpu, memory
```

However, the current affect if we had this:

```
insert cpu cpu.percent=80
```

and then issued this query:

```
select "cpu.percent" from cpu
```

It would fail, is it interpreted the prefix of `cpu.` as the measurement name.

We will need support for this in the future, but currently the query engine nor the query language support it.

I would suggest that to add it in the future, we parse anything inside quotes as a `VarRef`, so that:

`select "foo.bin.bar" from foo`

Will always see the field name `foo.bin.bar`.  But if we want it prefixed, then

`select foo."bin.bar" from foo`

would parse as the measurement `foo` and the field `bin.bar`.

@pauldix @dgnorton thoughts?

select sum(field1), sum(field2) from measurement where field2 > 0

title: Problem on continuous query with small group by
body:
Hi there,

I have tried to find a similar problem but I want to avoid hijacking a thread if this is not related.

I have a database with quite a lot of metrics sent from riemann, I am using CQ to downsample my metrics which are pretty easy:

```
_1h
"CREATE CONTINUOUS QUERY _1h ON db1 BEGIN SELECT mean(value) AS "value" INTO "db1"."_1h".:MEASUREMENT FROM "db1"."default"./.*/ GROUP BY time(1m), host END"
_1d
"CREATE CONTINUOUS QUERY _1d ON db1 BEGIN SELECT mean(value) AS "value" INTO "db1"."_1d".:MEASUREMENT FROM "db1"."default"./.*/ GROUP BY time(5m), host END"
_1w
"CREATE CONTINUOUS QUERY _1w ON db1 BEGIN SELECT mean(value) AS "value" INTO "db1"."_1w".:MEASUREMENT FROM "db1"."default"./.*/ GROUP BY time(30m), host END"
_4w
"CREATE CONTINUOUS QUERY _4w ON db1 BEGIN SELECT mean(value) AS "value" INTO "db1"."_4w".:MEASUREMENT FROM "db1"."_1d"./.*/ GROUP BY time(2h), host END"
_24w
"CREATE CONTINUOUS QUERY _24w ON db1 BEGIN SELECT mean(value) AS "value" INTO "db1"."_24w".:MEASUREMENT FROM "db1"."_1d"./.*/ GROUP BY time(12h), host END"
_52w
"CREATE CONTINUOUS QUERY _52w ON db1 BEGIN SELECT mean(value) AS "value" INTO "db1"."_52w".:MEASUREMENT FROM "db1"."_1w"./.*/ GROUP BY time(1d), host END"
```

I am running influxdb 0.9.5.1, when I check the logs I can see that the CQ are correctly executed.

The problem I am facing is that inside the _1h retention policy I am missing series for some hosts. It seems to have happened since I have more and more hosts sending data, hence more metrics.

I have tried to play around with the variables of [continuous_queries] but I have trouble to understand their role. 

What I think is happening is that they are too much data to compute for that CQ to run all at once and everything is not computed at the same time. So next time the CQ runs it tries to go and have a look at what is not computed but it is considered as lagged and not treated ?

Could I be correct?

Thanks for your help.

One variation doesn't work and I am curious if my test is correct or not.

title: Query with order by time DESC fail with WAL
body:
When doing a query like "SELECT value FROM cpu_load_short ORDER BY time DESC LIMIT 1", I don't always get the last value.

From what I see, I get the last value from data dir, not the one in WAL. There is a special case, when data dir is empty, WAL is effectively used.

To reproduce this issue, I just need to write fast enough to keep data in WAL:

1) rm -fr ~/.influxdb
2) ./usr/bin/influxd (I used standalone binary, 0.9.6, 0.9.6.1 and 0.10.0-nightly-4f65dc0)
3) Run the following

```
count=1
curl -G http://localhost:8086/query --data-urlencode "q=CREATE DATABASE mydb"

while true; do curl -i -XPOST 'http://localhost:8086/write?db=mydb' --data-binary "cpu_load_short,host=server01,region=us-west value=$count ${count}000000000"; echo; sleep 0.1;count=$(($count + 1));done
```

4) Keep the loop running, "SELECT value FROM cpu_load_short ORDER BY time DESC LIMIT 1" will return the last entry (we only write in WAL)

title: Loosing series merging when performing a rollup
body:
I'm trying to use continuous queries to perform rollups (trying to achieve something similar to #5335 or #5234)

I'm using something like `CREATE CONTINUOUS QUERY mycq ON mydb BEGIN SELECT mean(value) AS mean_value INTO mydb_5m.fortydays.:MEASUREMENT FROM mydb.oneday./mymeasurement/ GROUP BY time(5m), * END` to aggregate my data. 

Then `SELECT mean_value from mymeasurement` (using `mydb_5m`) returns a data point _per serie_ for every 5m period, where I'd want it to return a single point: the mean of the merged series for that 5m period.
The same happens if we filter only by a subset of `mymeasurement`'s tag set: we get as many points per 5m period as the number of combinations of the tags we didn't specify.

This is solved easily when we aggregate using a sum, as we can sum sums, but it doesn't mean anything anymore if we're trying to combine means or percentiles.

In other words, we loose series merging when performing a rollup, and I can't see an easy way to work around this. All I can think of is to add a continuous query per most-used tag combination, but it can be quite cumbersome.

title: Consider using seconds as the default precision
body:
InfluxDB currently defaults to nanosecond precision for writes and queries. Most other tools and languages use second precision. Given that
- a common beginner mistake is using timestamps with second precision (resulting in a bunch of 1970 points that trip people up), and
- significant compression gains can be realized when using seconds as the precision with the TSM engine,

Should we consider changing the default precision for timestamps to seconds?

For reference, the default precision is set here:
https://github.com/influxdata/influxdb/blob/master/models/points.go#L1241

title: nested or sub query support
body:
This is a feature request / discussion about if it's even feasible to do nested or "sub" queries.

I have a use case where I would like to combine several different series (in different measurements and with different tags) into one "value" with one query (or nested query). I would then be able to display this one single value in existing dashboards like Chronograf or Grafana.

As an example to explain why this might be useful, imagine several machines as part of a complex system reporting transaction latency, where a transaction crosses three servers: A -> B -> C. Each of these metrics is a collected into a different series. What would be nice is single query to show the total latency of the transaction. Doing this in (normal) SQL would look something like:

```
SELECT A.value + B.value + C.value AS total_latency
FROM (SELECT value from SeriesA) AS A,
(SELECT value from SeriesB) AS B,
(SELECT value from SeriesC) AS C
```

Of course such a feature would probably add a lot of complexity to InfluxDB, and moves it a little more towards it being a data processing engine, so I can understand if you don't want to consider such a feature.

The workaround is to use some external App / Script to do the three queries independently and munge the data together to get the total result. That makes it a lot harder to add into pretty dashboards though.

title: [Feature Request] COUNT(): return zeros instead of no results
body:
### Feature Request

**Proposal:** Provide a way to return zeros for count() queries instead of no results.

**Current behavior:** (Note: this feature request is a followup to what I mistakenly thought was a bug. That github issue is here: https://github.com/influxdata/influxdb/issues/6400)

Check out these two simple queries. The first query returns zeros for all of the grouped minutes for which there are no observations to count. That is the expected behavior -- return zero when there are no observations to count. The second query returns no results at all. That seems incorrect. The two queries only differ in the time part of the WHERE clause, but there is time overlap between them.

```
> SELECT COUNT("myField") FROM "myMeasurement" WHERE time > 1460757540000000000 AND time < 1460757840000000000 GROUP BY TIME(1m)
name: myMeasurement
------------------------
time                count
1460757540000000000 0
1460757600000000000 0
1460757660000000000 19
1460757720000000000 0
1460757780000000000 0

> SELECT COUNT("myField") FROM "myMeasurement" WHERE time > 1460757720000000000 AND time < 1460757840000000000 GROUP BY TIME(1m)
>
```

**Desired behavior:** Instead of not returning any results I would like the second query to return zeros:

```
name: myMeasurement
------------------------
time                count
1460757720000000000 0
1460757780000000000 0
```

**Possible Implementation:** @jsternberg mentiond in https://github.com/influxdata/influxdb/issues/6400 that, "In order to know what series need to be filled in, there needs to be at least one point with that name/tag combination. Since tags can be any arbitrary combination, it's impossible for us to know which combinations to fill without having some basis."

**Perhaps an optional windowing period could be passed to count() to generate the list of tag combinations that could then be filled if missing?** 

**Use case:** This is rendering my Kapacitor alerts, which only sometimes fire due to inconsistent zero counts vs. no results, essentially useless. Kapacitor alerts that test for "count" == 0 cannot be relied upon to trigger when expected. This doesn't seem like it's Kapacitor's fault -- Influx is only returning zeros in the groups when there is a data point in the window.

title: Don't catch SIGQUIT; safer close of Quit channel
body:
###### Required for all non-trivial PRs
- [x] Rebased/mergable
- [x] Tests pass
- [x] CHANGELOG.md updated

A `SIGQUIT` signal should indicate to a running process that it should exit immediately, and also dump its core. This is the default behaviour for a Go program, unless the program catches the signal using `signal.Notify`. 

We were catching this signal in `influx` and then attempting to exit gracefully, which is the incorrect behaviour, especially if `influx` is stuck somewhere, or in a long running query.

Also, we were catching other signals that didn't make sense, e.g., `SIGHUP`—usually used to indicate a live configuration change, `os.Kill`—we're not even allowed to catch this.

This PR reduces the signals we catch down to `syscall.SIGINT` and `syscall.SIGTERM`. It also ensure that the `Quit` channel is closed properly.

Helps to fix #6474

title: [feature]continuous query with time offset
body:
Here comes a common situation that data is written to influxdb with some latency(i.e. written with timestamp specified), and when we need to do some aggregation or downsampling on such data stream, we would like to run CQ every `<interval>` time , but with some offset or latency, i.e. we want to aggregate on data between `now()-latency-interval` and `now()-latency`, instead of between `now()-interval` and `now()`.

The only way I know to do such a job is to use `RESAMPLE FOR <LONG_DURATION>` in CQ query, but that may lead to useless workload for influxdb.

For example, we may need to do aggregation on data between `now()-60seconds` and `now()-50seconds` every `10seconds`, in CQ:

```
CREATE CONTINUOUS QUERY RESAMPLE FOR 60s BEGIN ... GROUP BY time(10s) END
```

However, such CQ leads to 6 queries on data `[now()-60s, now()-50s)`, `[now()-50s, now()-40s)`, `[now()-40s, now()-30s)`, `[now()-30s, now()-20s)`, `[now()-20s, now()-10s)`, `[now()-10s, now()`, where the only useful query is the first one.

title: [Feature Request] Time literal arithmetic
body:
### Feature Request

**Current behavior:** We can't use any expressions with time literals

title: [feature request] Limit number of series iterators for non-aggregate queries
body:
### Feature Request

**Proposal:** Add a way to limit the total number of series iterators opened at one time for a non-aggregate query.

**Current behavior:** Non-aggregate queries create an iterator for each series, which can lead to unbounded memory usage for queries that pull from many series at once.

**Desired behavior:** Limit the number of series iterators a query can create to prevent runaway memory use and out of memory errors, while still allowing an answer to be returned eventually.

**Use case:** A naive query, like `SELECT * FROM cpu`, will result in a spike to memory usage until the query finishes. Depending on available memory and the number of series selected, the memory spike can result in the OS killing the InfluxDB process with an out of memory error.

Note that this behavior is different from the [`max-select-series`](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/v0.13/troubleshooting/query_management/#max-select-series) setting since a result should still eventually be returned.

cc @benbjohnson @jsternberg

title: discussion: Should multiple selectors in a query return more than one line of results?
body:
### Feature Request

**Proposal:** [Description of the feature]

`SELECT LAST(foo), MAX(bar), FIRST(baz)...` should return three lines in the result, not one. That way the actual timestamp for each point can be provided.

**Current behavior:** [What currently happens]

Given these points:

```
> select * from selector
name: selector
--------------
time            bar baz foo
1469126083643297249 1   15  12
1469126089187079301 12  12  1
1469126100199191932 42  42  42
1469126128754879528 2   0   22
```

The return from three selectors has no meaningful timestamps:

```
> SELECT LAST(foo), MAX(bar), FIRST(baz) FROM selector
name: selector
--------------
time    last    max first
0   22  42  15
```

**Desired behavior:** [What you would like to happen]
Instead, what if the return were as follows:

```
> SELECT LAST(foo), MAX(bar), FIRST(baz) FROM selector
name: selector
--------------
time    last    max first
1469126128754879528 22  
1469126100199191932     42  
1469126083643297249         15
```

**Use case:** [Why is this important (helps with prioritizing requests)]

Right now, multiple selectors in a single query returns only the field values, not a timestamp. Selectors are returning a single point, so the timestamp is often meaningful information. We can reduce overall queries for systems if multiple selectors can be used in a single query, rather than forcing users to do `SELECT LAST(foo)...; SELECT MAX(bar)...; SELECT FIRST(baz)...`

**System info:**

Commit: f0db39037796e2c501785b8dfb6e570d5b645c20
Build: 1.0.0-c1.0.0
**4 node cluster**

**Steps to reproduce:**
- Assuming you have a 4 node cluster
- Create two databases, one with replication factor == # nodes and one that is not.

```
CREATE DATABASE "TestRepl4" WITH DURATION INF REPLICATION 4 NAME "RP_TestRepl4"
CREATE DATABASE "TestRepl2" WITH DURATION INF REPLICATION 2 NAME "RP_TestRepl2"
```
- Insert dummy data into both

```
USE TestRepl4
INSERT INTO RP_TestRepl4 treasures,captain_id=pirate_king value=2

USE TestRepl2
INSERT INTO RP_TestRepl2 treasures,captain_id=pirate_king value=2
```
- Select using `FROM /.*/` on...

The database with replication factor == # of nodes

```
USE TestRepl4
select value from /.*/ where captain_id='pirate_king'
```

.. and you get data

However, select from the database with replication factor != # of nodes..

```
USE TestRepl2
select value from /.*/ where captain_id='pirate_king'

Note that specifying the measurement in the `TestRepl2` does indeed return the data as expected.

```

Without a way to specify read quorum for a cluster. Why then provide the option of Replication factor for a database at all when surely all users would want replication factor == node?

title: Allocation/pointer removal
body:
###### Required for all non-trivial PRs
- [x] Rebased/mergable
- [x] Tests pass
- [x] CHANGELOG.md updated
- [x] Sign [CLA](https://influxdata.com/community/cla/) (if not already signed)

This PR has a few changes to remove pointers and allocations.

* There are several long running goroutines that would `time.Sleep` every second.  This ends up allocating as seen by `GODEBUG=allocfreetrace=1`.  These were replaced with `time.Timer` which avoids the allocation and is more idiomatic.
* `findGenerations` is called a lot and ends up allocation quite a bit when many shards exists.  The result is usually the same because the generations do not change until a compaction completes.  This caches the result to avoid all the re-allocations.
* Converts all the `*Value` types to be non-pointers.   They don't need to be pointers since they are immutable once created.

title: Support subquery execution in the query language
body:
This adds query syntax support for subqueries and adds support to the
query engine to execute queries on subqueries.

Subqueries act as a source for another query. It is the equivalent of
writing the results of a query to a temporary database, executing
a query on that temporary database, and then deleting the database
(except this is all performed in-memory).

The syntax is like this:

    SELECT sum(derivative) FROM (SELECT derivative(mean(value)) FROM cpu GROUP BY *)

This will execute derivative and then sum the result of those derivatives.
Another example:

    SELECT max(min) FROM (SELECT min(value) FROM cpu GROUP BY host)

This would let you find the maximum minimum value of each host.

There is complete freedom to mix subqueries with auxiliary fields. The only
caveat is that the following two queries:

    SELECT mean(value) FROM cpu
    SELECT mean(value) FROM (SELECT value FROM cpu)

Have different performance characteristics. The first will calculate
`mean(value)` at the shard level and will be faster, especially when it comes to
clustered setups. The second will process the mean at the top level and will not
include that optimization.

Fixes #4619.

title: Difference(aggregate(field)) requires lower time boundary
body:
Tested on: nightly  `1.2.0~n201612120800`

SELECT statements running `difference(aggregate(field))` require a lower time boundary in order to return results.

```
> select difference(mean(ELEC)) from elecquantity where time < '2016-01-01T00:05:00Z' and groupuuid = 'e11c9dc87176ba67f1a3463ca2f707b5e58f7ba2' group by time(1m)
>

The statement works when the lower time boundary is set:

```
> select difference(mean(ELEC)) from elecquantity where time >= '2016-01-01T00:00:00Z' and time < '2016-01-01T00:05:00Z' and groupuuid = 'e11c9dc87176ba67f1a3463ca2f707b5e58f7ba2' group by time(1m)

2016-01-01T00:01:00Z 10

This feature was implemented per https://github.com/influxdata/influxdb/issues/1825 and used to work without a lower time boundary in older versions e.g. v0.13:

b) select t1,max(f1),min(f2) from m1 where t1='aa'

__Expected behavior:__

In both cases, t1 should be available to select.

title: Feature request: InfluxQL comments
body:
__Proposal:__ Comments in InfluxQL.

__Current behavior:__ Comments are not supported.

__Desired behavior:__ Allow line-oriented comments in InfluxQL. Example:

```
# This query computes a bar from foo.
select bar from foo
```

__Use case:__ When performing data analysis, I end up using scripting pipelines that look like this:
```
cat my_query.infuxql | influx > output.txt
```

title: Allow single value to be repeated in query result
body:
### Feature Request

__Proposal:__ [Description of the feature]

Repeating a value is often useful or graphing or somehow inspecting data. This value could be a constant, but will typically be derived from the data in query result.

Further, some visualizations tools (grafana, AFAICT) does not allow the extension of a single point into a time series, while others do.

__Current behavior:__ [What currently happens]

When selecting a single value (max/min/mean/avg/percentile) over a time series, the value is returned for a single time in the middle of the selected time (a point in time). The value however is not representative for that time, but for a selected interval of time.

__Desired behavior:__ [What you would like to happen]

SELECT REPEAT(percentile(some_value, 95)) FROM ...

The single value will then be added is a column to each timestamp.

"repeat" is a suggested name. Could be constant or extend or similar.

Allowing injection of value might also be useful, e.g.:

SELECT REPEAT (4) as four, value FROM ...

But not so sure about that one.

__Use case:__ [Why is this important (helps with prioritizing requests)]

Showing an aggregated value for a certain interval can be quite helpful for certain applications. E.g., 95/98 percentile is a very commonly used metric in networking. Getting it as a single value is not ideal.

There is probably a discussion here about how customizable the data from influxdb should be and how much functionality should be in the upper layers. With a grafana + influxdb setup, the functionality sort of falls between chairs (I might have missed some functionality).

title: Allow meaningful use of duration literals in expressions
body:
### Feature Request

Opening a feature request kicks off a discussion.
Requests may be closed if we're not actively planning to work on them.

__Proposal:__

Allow duration literals (such as `1m`, `1s` etc.) in `SELECT` expressions to allow computing various specific values.

__Current behavior:__

Let's suppose I have a netflow collector that inserts each flow into InfluxDB as a data point, recording actual traffic amount (in bytes) as fields:
```
> select "bytes_in", "bytes_out" from "lan.9-20.router.wan" where time > now() - 1m20s
name: lan.9-20.router.wan
time                        bytes_in bytes_out
----                        -------- ---------
2017-03-17T14:10:09.000135Z 3155     530
2017-03-17T14:10:09.000294Z 264      154
2017-03-17T14:10:09.000306Z 80       120
2017-03-17T14:10:09.000493Z 3157     530
2017-03-17T14:10:10.000102Z 2372     5491
<...>
```

I can use a `GROUP BY` statement to select aggregate traffic over arbitrary time windows:
```
> select sum("bytes_in"), sum("bytes_out") from "lan.9-20.router.wan" where time > now() - 5m group by time(1m)
name: lan.9-20.router.wan
time                 sum     sum_1
----                 ---     -----
2017-03-17T14:07:00Z 201499  381059
2017-03-17T14:08:00Z 212015  228125
2017-03-17T14:09:00Z 1196106 1139874
2017-03-17T14:10:00Z 288895  713716
2017-03-17T14:11:00Z 40414   39110
```

Now imagine that I want to select aggregate traffic _rate_ (in bytes/s) over these time windows. This means I need to divide the sum by the grouping interval (it it substituted via `$interval` in Grafana, so I cannot just write "60" there):

```
> select (sum("bytes_in") + sum("bytes_out")) / (1m / 1s) from "lan.9-20.router.wan" where time > now() - 5m group by time(1m)
ERR: unable to construct an iterator from two literals: LHS: *influxql.DurationLiteral, RHS: *influxql.DurationLiteral
```

I write `1m / 1s` to avoid a unit mismatch (dividing a dimensionless quantity by time quantity is mathematically meaningless).

__Desired behavior:__

I want InfluxDB to handle expressions like `1m / 1s`, yielding a dimensionless quantity (e. g. 60):

```
> select (sum("bytes_in") + sum("bytes_out")) / (1m / 1s) from "lan.9-20.router.wan" where time > now() - 5m group by time(1m)
name: lan.9-20.router.wan
time                 sum_sum
----                 -------
2017-03-17T14:18:00Z 1545.2333333333333
2017-03-17T14:19:00Z 31719.816666666666
2017-03-17T14:20:00Z 6771.4
2017-03-17T14:21:00Z 6256.716666666666
2017-03-17T14:22:00Z 4136.6
2017-03-17T14:23:00Z 1271.9166666666667
```

__Use case:__

This is important to users of Grafana, where one cannot just write "60" in query, but has to use the same `$interval` that one is grouping by:

```
> select (sum("bytes_in") + sum("bytes_out")) / ($interval / 1s) from "lan.9-20.router.wan" where time > now() - 5m group by time($interval)
```

title: Queries slow or never respond but only on certain days and when database reaches ~150G
body:
### Bug report

__System info:__ 
 version 1.2.1, branch master, commit 3ec60fe2649b51a85cd1db6c8937320a80a64c35

__Steps to reproduce:__
Note: This bug report follows community case: https://community.influxdata.com/t/strange-query-issues-when-database-reaches-140g/297/19

Background: 

- We are using Influx to store time series data for the last 5 working days (i.e. 7 day retention but with no data recorded on weekends).
- We aggregate data from 30+ different sources and there is a high degree of back-filling.
- Cardinality is ~5200.
- Typical queries:
-- Count the records in a specified 1 minute time period, from a specified source. 
-- Select all tags and queries using the same criteria and returning 1000 records (limit).

1. I populate influx database by running my server.
2. I let database reach about 80% loaded, which is equal to about 150G on disk.
3. I perform some queries to examine the data.

__Expected behavior:__ 
I expect "count" queries to return in 300ms or less and "select 1000" queries to return in 3000ms or less.

__Actual behavior:__ [What actually happened]
Many of the queries return within spec. However, I am also finding one day in five where data retrieval is either very slow or not successful.  When this happens, memory usage typically starts crawling up to 90% at which point kswap0 starts getting very active.  

So, for example, 

- My database has 5 days worth of data: 2017 March 21, 22, 23, 24 & 27.
- It occupies 151Gb (according to 'du' display)
- 1000 rows of data can be retrieved under 3 seconds but only if retrieved from days 21, 22, 23 and 27.
- If I try and select all tags & fields for any time period on March 24, it never returns and memory/cpu on the influx machine gradually increases.
- If I try doing a "select count(field)" for the same time period, I can sometimes (after about 10 seconds) get a count number back. However, it does not work for all fields, only some.
- Furthermore, if I do a select on only one field for the same time period it can work, but again only after several seconds.


__Additional info:__ [Include gist of relevant config, logs, etc.]

There is no obvious error reporting to the influxdb.log.

See https://gist.github.com/billevans1963/e4c0ad09ce457c78dde6573eed303924

For example, this query, which returns 659 lines runs in 120~150 ms:
`SELECT last("ServiceStatus") as ServiceStatus FROM "DefaultPaulo"."ServiceStats" WHERE "Environment" =~ /^PT02$/ AND Time > now() - 7m AND ServiceName != 'Asos.Service.Emailer' AND ServiceName != 'Asos.Stock.DespatchImportService' AND ServiceName != 'Asos.Stock.StockExportService' AND ServiceStartType <> 4 GROUP BY "ServiceName", "host"`

While this simple SELECT FROM the same query with a trivial WHERE, runs in 4~5 seconds:
`SELECT host, ServiceName, ServiceStatus FROM (`
`SELECT last("ServiceStatus") as ServiceStatus FROM "DefaultPaulo"."ServiceStats" WHERE "Environment" =~ /^PT02$/ AND Time > now() - 7m AND ServiceName != 'Asos.Service.Emailer' AND ServiceName != 'Asos.Stock.DespatchImportService' AND ServiceName != 'Asos.Stock.StockExportService' AND ServiceStartType <> 4 GROUP BY "ServiceName", "host"`
`) WHERE "ServiceStatus" <> 4`

---
...
---

I do know things like the Regex expression filters can naturally perform poorly due to the underlying complexity of regex searches. However, both of those things are performing just fine in the inner query - 120~150ms.

The nested query, though, is adding very minimal work on top of the inner query, not justifying making it 30 times slower... It's applying 1 single WHERE filter against the only selected field. I can't conceive any reason for that 2nd layer of querying to add such a performance hit: we're talking of 660 lines of data, and the field "ServiceStatus" will only have some 2~5 different values, which is what's making me guess this is a performance problem.

title: Client subscriptions
body:
### Feature Request

__Proposal:__ [Description of the feature]
It would be nice if InfluxDB had a subscription feature more designed for clients than the current "push everything" model kapacitor uses.
A client might want to receive specific new points as they come in. Right now the only way to do this is if the client sets up a listening socket, and then tells InfluxDB to publish everything it receives to that socket. The downsides to this are:
1. InfluxDB initiates a new connection. Meaning the client has to set up a listening socket, and has to be reachable from InfluxDB. This latter point is a big issue when you have firewalls and such in the way.
2. The client has to make sure to tear down the subscription when done. If the client leaves ungracefully (network loss, crash, etc), the subscription will remain and InfluxDB will keep trying to connect to it indefinitely.
Instead the data for the subscription should be sent over the same socket the subscription request was issued on.
3. The client has to do point filtering and perform field operations (math, derivative, etc). Since the current subscription design sends everything, the client doesn't have the ability to apply a simple `WHERE` clause on the points and only receive what it's interested in. Aside from more work the client has to do, if the database receives a lot of data, but the client is only interested in a small amount, it could flood the network with useless data. Especially if there are many clients trying to do such a subscription.
Obviously some types of operations might be problematic/impossible? for a subscription, such as a `GROUP BY`. So I think it would be acceptable to say some operations are not allowed, at least for a v1 implementation.



__Current behavior:__ [What currently happens]
Currently to be able to accomplish the end goal of receiving points as they come in to InfluxDB, the client has to implement a polling mechanism, sending `SELECT` queries every X (milli)seconds.

__Desired behavior:__ [What you would like to happen]
Client should be able to receive points instantly as they come in.

__Use case:__ [Why is this important (helps with prioritizing requests)]
So applications can receive data as it comes in without doing a ton of extra work, and work which InfluxDB already does.

title: Need to be able to disconnect dead clients
body:
### Feature Request

__Proposal:__
InfluxDB needs to have a way to detect and disconnect dead (or possibly even idle) clients.

__Current behavior:__
If a client has an open connection to InfluxDB, but that client ungracefully disconnects (e.g. crash or network disconnection), the socket on influxDB's side remains open forever. Eventually the server can accumulate hundreds or thousands of these sockets, exhausting available file descriptors.

__Desired behavior:__
InfluxDB either needs to support configuration of [TCP KeepAlive](https://golang.org/pkg/net/#TCPConn.SetKeepAlive), and/or the server needs a simple configuration parameter for a request timeout where it closes the connection after idle for X seconds).

According to the documentation, version 0.8 had a `read-timeout` parameter that satisfied this requirement: https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/v0.8/advanced_topics/configuration_options/

__Use case:__
If a client has an open connection to InfluxDB, but that client ungracefully disconnects (e.g. crash or network disconnection), the socket on influxDB's side remains open forever. Eventually the server can accumulate hundreds or thousands of these sockets, exhausting available file descriptors.

title: Implement basic trigonometry functions
body:
This adds support for math functions into the query language. Math
functions are special because they are transformations and do not access
the filesystem in the same way aggregate functions do. A transformation
takes one point and always outputs one point making it more similar to
binary expressions so these math functions follow the same rules as
binary expressions.

This also supports using math literals (so you can do `sin(1)`) and the
math functions can be used anywhere such as in a field or an expression.
Both of the following are supported:

    SELECT sin(value) FROM cpu
    SELECT value FROM cpu WHERE sin(value) > 0.5

Arguments are in radians. Degrees is not supported.

Fixes #9424.
