title: New `tap` subcommand v1
body:
As part of https://github.com/timberio/vector-product/issues/24, we want to introduce a way for users to tap into a running Vector instance and sample events.

## Goals

1. Ability to sample events at any step within the configured pipeline.
2. Do so in a way that will unblock the web UI. The web UI will have sampling ability.

## Proposal

I propose that we introduce a new `vector tap` subcommand:

```bash

USAGE:
    vector tap [OPTIONS] [ID]

OPTIONS
    --limit            Exit when this limit is reached (no default)
    --position         Whether to tap at the front or back of the component (default front)

title: Ability to drop old and future data
body:
Vector needs the ability to drop old and future data. This helps protect against errors that could result in a high number of downstream indexes. For example, if a date is incorrectly extracted this could result in many dates spanning many days. This would subsequently create many downstream indexes/partitions which would not be good for systems like Elasticsearch where this could affect stability.

It's not clear to me how we should implement this just yet, but a few ideas:

1. Global settings that discards data outside of a configured window regardless of the source.
2. Per source settings.
3. A transform that all sources must run through.
4. Per sink settings.

I'm leaning towards 1 to start, since this is the easiest and makes the most sense from a goal standpoint. The goal being to discard stale or data far into the future.

title: prometheus_scrape source or prometheus_exporter sink does not expire values
body:
I'm not sure if the issue here is with the sink or the source, but a user in discord brought up that the last successful scrape value for a metric scraped by the `prometheus_scrape` source was being returned even after the node went away.

https://discord.com/channels/742820443487993987/746070591097798688/796088208386818148

### Vector Version

<!---
Run `vector --version` to show the version, and paste the result between the ``` marks below.

If you are not running the latest version of Vector, please try upgrading because your issue may have already been fixed.
-->

```
vector 0.11.1 (v0.11.1 x86_64-unknown-linux-musl 2020-12-17)
```

### Vector Configuration File

<!--
Paste the relevant parts of your `vector.toml` configuration between the ``` marks below.

!! If your config files contain sensitive information please remove it !!
-->

```toml
[sources.prometheus]
type = "prometheus_scrape"
endpoints = ["http://localhost:9100/metrics"]

[sinks.out]
type = "prometheus_exporter"
inputs = ["prometheus"]
address = "0.0.0.0:9598" # required
```

### Debug Output
```
Jan 05 19:02:36.557  INFO vector::app: Log level is enabled. level="vector=info,codec=info,file_source=info,tower_limit=trace,rdkafka=info"
Jan 05 19:02:36.557  INFO vector::app: Loading configs. path=[("in.toml", None)]
Jan 05 19:02:36.559  INFO vector::topology: Running healthchecks.
Jan 05 19:02:36.559  INFO vector::topology: Starting source. name="prometheus"
Jan 05 19:02:36.559  INFO vector::topology: Starting sink. name="out"
Jan 05 19:02:36.559  INFO vector::topology::builder: Healthcheck: Passed.
Jan 05 19:02:36.559  INFO vector: Vector has started. version="0.11.1" git_version="v0.11.1" released="Thu, 17 Dec 2020 17:03:52 +0000" arch="x86_64"
Jan 05 19:02:36.559  INFO vector::app: API is disabled, enable by setting `api.enabled` to `true` and use commands like `vector top`.
Jan 05 19:03:06.568 ERROR source{component_kind="source" component_name=prometheus component_type=prometheus_scrape}: vector::internal_events::prometheus: HTTP request processing error. url=http://localhost:9100/metrics error=CallRequest { source: hyper::Error(Connect, ConnectError("tcp connect error", Os { code: 111, kind: ConnectionRefused, message: "Connection refused" })) }
```

### Expected Behavior

`curl`ing the `prometheus_exporter` endpoint after the `prometheus_scrape` source fails to pull metrics should result in those metrics not being returned anymore; otherwise they are stale.

### Actual Behavior

The `prometheus_exporter` endpoint continues to return the last scraped value.

### Reproduce

* Start `node_exporter` (https://prometheus.io/docs/guides/node-exporter/)
* Start `vector` with above config
* `curl localhost:9598/metrics` and note the metrics are there
* Stop the `node_exporter`
* Wait for vector to output a scrape error
* `curl localhost:9598/metrics` and note that the metrics are still there

title: Improve Vector's throughput for UDP protocols
body:
Currently we process UDP packets serially in the `syslog` source when mode `udp` is used:

https://github.com/timberio/vector/blob/410fac0b7fbb0c7361056105ba362f7ee6c112ca/src/sources/syslog.rs#L422-L444

It seems like we should be able to improve throughput introducing concurrency here given that processing the packet does involve some decoding and parsing work.

This is also true for the `socket` source:

https://github.com/vectordotdev/vector/blob/801ee2178b8e30d2695a131185e09b11c7623ffd/src/sources/socket/udp.rs#L92

Perhaps one worker per "connection" similar to the `tcp` mode where we could use a source ip/port pair to partition them; or just by having a fixed (configurable?) number of workers processing packets.

title: Vector crash on corrupt disk buffer
body:
A user in Slack ran into a situation where Vector crashed when starting up complaining about an invalid disk buffer. Unfortunately we lost the stack trace, but the error message included "corrupted compressed block contents".

I imagine this could happen in the case where there is a hard stop mid-write or mid-delete. 

I did discover that leveldb has the ability to repair itself (https://docs.rs/leveldb/0.8.6/leveldb/database/management/fn.repair.html) so we could do this either when we see this error or, in an abundance of caution, on every vector boot (if it is not an expensive operation).

title: `aws_s3` source now has an unconfigurable cap on line length
body:
A user in discord [reported](https://discord.com/channels/742820443487993987/746070591097798688/897956301693419550) that when they upgraded to 0.17.0 that messages started being dropped:

```
{"buf_len":111975,"internal_log_rate_secs":30,"max_length":102400,"message":"Discarding frame larger than max_length.","metadata":{"kind":"event","level":"WARN","module_path":"vector::codecs::framers::character_delimited","target":"vector::codecs::framers::character_delimited"}
```

This appears to be because in https://github.com/vectordotdev/vector/commit/bd426029c5#diff-ce8ca490d9ddbe754a3227df21f669c2f7c95198ca26c9067076ad364617bbcdR411 the previous `BytesDelimitedCodec` which had a default `max_length` of `usize::max` was replaced by `CharacterDelimitedCodec` which has a lower default limit of 100kib.
